items.title: Neela Badami joins NLSIU as Professor of Practice
items.summary: Neela Badami has joined National Law School of India University (NLSIU), Bengaluru as Professor of Practice. Neela holds a B.A.LL.B (Hons) from National Academy of Legal Studies and Research (NALSAR) University of Law and an LL.M. from the University of Michigan Law School, where she was a Michigan Grotius Scholar. Formerly, she was an equity partner at Samvad Partners . She has advised investors, founders, and companies on private equity, venture capital, mergers & acquisitions. Over the years, she has advised funds, startups and corporates across sectors. She had earlier stints at Amarchand Mangaldas (now CAM) (Capital Markets) and the International Criminal Court in The Hague.

items.title: At COP17, the fight is to give women more than a seat at the biodiversity table
items.summary: In 1730, when soldiers arrived in Khejarli village in Rajasthan to fell trees for a royal palace, Amrita Devi Bishnoi wrapped her arms around a Khejri tree to protect it. She was killed, along with 362 others from the Bishnoi community, in an act of resistance that helped bring the tree-felling to a halt. More than two centuries later, in Uttarakhand, Gaura Devi and 27 women embraced trees in Reni village in 1974 to prevent the felling of about 1,000 trees. In Assam, the Hargila Army, founded in 2007 by conservationist Purnima Devi Barman, continues to mobilise rural women to protect the endangered greater adjutant stork and its nesting trees. From protecting sacred trees in Rajasthan to conserving forests in Uttarakhand and saving endangered birds in Assam, women across India have shaped the fight to protect biodiversity. Yet, their knowledge, leadership, and contributions do not always translate into an equal say in decisions about how nature is conserved, who controls natural resources, and where conservation funding goes. However, the petition has been before the top court's registry since September 1 owing to defects.
